article_title: The Effect of Contextual and Conceptual Rewording on Mathematical Problem-Solving Performance
citation: Majid Haghverdi and Lynda R. Wiest. (2016). The Effect of Contextual and Conceptual Rewording on Mathematical Problem-Solving Performance. The Mathematics Educator, 25(1), 56–73. https://matheducator
title: Four-test instrument (T0–T3) of six two-step word problems with Knifong and Holtan error scoring
description: The first author developed four paper-and-pencil mathematics tests. Test T0, the original unmodified test, served as the pretest for all groups and the control group's posttest; Tests T1, T2, and T3 were reworded versions matching contextual, conceptual, and combined rewording. T0 consisted of six two-step arithmetic word problems from Iran's standard seventh-grade textbook, selected by five mathematics head teachers via the Delphi method for unfamiliar context and little contextualizing description. Each problem was scored 0–2 for error type, so test scores ranged 0–12.
requirements: Problems selected had to be unfamiliar or minimally familiar and offer little description of key problem elements; reworded versions were developed by the same five head teachers
constraints: Problems were drawn from Iranian textbooks, so cultural and linguistic context would need consideration in similar research elsewhere
examples: Each experimental group of 20 completed the same pretest but a different posttest; error categories followed Knifong and Holtan's (1976) classification.
